parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence and no documented visitor-facing measure (entry/document checks, facility rules, custody placement) appear; same-sex conduct has been legal since 1998 and no trans visitor detention is recorded — these hold the score up. Against that: documented police extortion of LGBTQ people (2018), monitoring showing high stigma concentrated in law enforcement, frequent reported discrimination and violence with a near-300% rise in attacks after the 2014 anti-LGBT reforms, a 2025 legislative/transphobic media campaign, contracted public LGBTQ life, and no non-discrimination statute or working remedy. Resident-facing losses (LGR removed 2021, age-25 care floor, 2026 draft at first reading) are climate signals only.

entry_documents.exposure: No documented border friction, marker-mismatch screening, X-marker refusal, or device search practice for trans visitors. Visitors carry home-country documents; the 2021 removal of legal gender recognition touches residents, not foreign papers.
entry_documents.protection: Same-sex conduct decriminalised 1998; no documented entry refusal or secondary screening of transgender travellers.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry exposure is an open question: nothing in the dossier shows foreign documents doubted at the border, but nothing shows them accepted either.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Police reported in 2018 blackmailing LGBTQ people via social media and dating apps for sums of roughly 70–500 USD; monitoring records high stigma and discrimination concentrated in law enforcement.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No documented arrest, prosecution or detention of a transgender visitor; trans detainee placement and custody conditions are explicitly unsourced.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: App use or a mismatched ID during a stop could move a visitor into police hands where officers are documented perpetrators rather than protectors.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No facility, ward, restroom or custody-placement rule documented for visitors. Subnational record is limited to rural social ostracism (residents) and contracted public LGBTQ life in the capital.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Capital-versus-rural comparison beyond the ostracism finding is unrecorded; state treatment outside the capital is unknown.

care_services.exposure: Resident-facing: transition care barred below age 25 (2024 Clause 47 amendment); a 2026 draft banning gender-affirming care passed only first reading. A 2024 regional study covers trans migrants' access including HRT and HIV prevention.
care_services.protection: No documented refusal of emergency or routine care to a trans visitor.
care_services.interaction: A visitor needing care while outed would meet a system with no non-discrimination statute and law enforcement recorded as the least accepting institution.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: 2025 review records anti-LGBT legislative pushes plus a media campaign of homophobic and transphobic statements by MPs; an MP called for pride marchers to be beaten (2019); child-protection amendments (2023) vaguely restrict content on 'non-traditional sexual relations'; attacks rose nearly 300% after the 2014 reform drive.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Other deputies condemned the 2019 remarks; same-sex activity is legal.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing raises both the probability of outing and the severity of social and police responses to an outed visitor.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented for visitors. The 2026 draft would prohibit marker change and affirming care including for minors, but has passed only first reading; the 2024 care floor (age 25) is resident-facing.
minors_guardians.interaction: Child-protection content restrictions have undefined terms and do not mention sexual orientation, so their reach over a visiting parent and child is unresolved.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Reports of discrimination and violence against LGBTQ people are described as frequent, with a near-300% increase in attacks following 2014 anti-LGBT legal reforms; the capital's only gay club closed in 2017 as public life contracted.
street_violence_police_response.protection: No documented trans-specific killings or organised campaign; no documented pattern of attacks on foreign visitors.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: An outed visitor has no statute to invoke and no safe queer venue to fall back on; police are part of the problem per monitoring data.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No non-discrimination statute protecting LGBTQ people is described; no legal gender recognition since 2021; no documented working remedy for a visitor facing service refusal or police extortion.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Same-sex conduct legal since 1998 at age 16; no trans-specific criminal offence on the books.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Thin formal recourse compounds every other exposure: harassment, extortion and violence have no documented avenue a short-term visitor could actually use.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra has a routine, universal visitor-facing exclusion regime with denied admission and no remedy. This dossier documents no visitor-facing state measure at all — no register, no entry bar, no report requirement. Its exposure is street- and police-level rather than administrative and inescapable, so this case sits above 0.35-A despite comparably hostile official framing.

Kestrel Isles documents routine secondary screening, discretionary refusal and slow remedies at the border — a real universal-exposure axis. This dossier documents no border exposure but a worse police and social climate (documented police extortion, frequent violence, no statute). Losing a documented entry-exposure axis while gaining documented police predation puts this case moderately below 0.55-B.

Meridia has trained border staff, a tribunal, counsel access and compensation — operative protections plus only brief detention. Here there are no such protections: monitoring names law enforcement as the hostile actor, no non-discrimination statute exists, and remedies are undocumented. The absence of any working protection and presence of police extortion place this case materially below 0.75-C.

Meridia combines terminal police extortion, overnight cells, a dismissive oversight board and short jail terms — routine state-level shakedowns against travellers. This dossier has one dated (2018) police extortion report plus stigma findings, but no documented detention, no routine transit shakedowns and no custody placement. Less frequent and less state-continuous, so this case sits above 0.25-B.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime has no visitor-facing legal machinery: no trans criminal offence, no documented border, facility or custody rule, no documented detention of a trans visitor — the principal upward pressures. Downward pressures are behavioural and institutional: police documented as extortionists toward LGBTQ people (2018), monitoring that names law enforcement as the most discriminatory institution, frequent reported discrimination and violence, a near-300% rise in attacks after the 2014 reform drive, a 2025 legislative and media hostility campaign, collapsed public LGBTQ life, and no non-discrimination statute or documented working remedy. Resident-facing losses (recognition removed 2021, age-25 care floor, 2026 draft at first reading) are climate signals of a state moving against trans people, not direct visitor exposures. A traveller therefore faces no automatic, inescapable state measure but also no protection if outed — street and police exposure with thin recourse, aggravated for anyone using dating apps or needing care. For an adult with a minor, no visitor-specific rule is documented; the child-protection content law's undefined scope is an open question, not an exposure. Severity sits at blackmail/discrimination/assault (2–3) rather than custody, but frequency is documented as elevated and recourse is near-absent, yielding Elevated Risk.
